articles.title: [SYNTHETIC] Catheter ablation of atrial fibrillation: where next?
articles.abstract: Catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation continues to evolve; this editorial discusses pulsed field ablation and recurrence monitoring.

articles.title: [SYNTHETIC] Insertable cardiac monitor detection of AF recurrence after pulsed field ablation
articles.abstract: Insertable cardiac monitors were implanted in 88 participants after pulsed field ablation for AF. Over a mean follow-up of 18 months, recurrence detected by the insertable cardiac monitor was 22%.

articles.title: [SYNTHETIC] Pulsed-field versus thermal ablation for paroxysmal atrial fibrillation: a randomized trial
articles.abstract: Background: Pulsed field ablation (PFA) is an alternative to thermal ablation. Methods: In this multicenter randomized trial, a total of 412 patients with paroxysmal atrial fibrillation were randomized 1:1 to PFA or radiofrequency ablation. Rhythm was assessed with 72-hour Holter monitoring. Results: During a median follow-up of 12 months, freedom from atrial arrhythmia was 78.2% with PFA versus 74.0% with radiofrequency ablation (HR 0.84, 95% CI 0.61-1.15; p = 0.27). Major complications occurred in 1.0% and 1.5%. Conclusions: PFA was noninferior. A limitation is the open-label design. NCT99000101.
